description: After SLSQP and greedy repair, fix centres and solve an LP for the optimal radii, keeping the LP result only if it verifies and beats the greedy sum.
Run random restarts for 40% of the time, then repeatedly swap a large and a small circle's positions in the best packing and re-optimise with SLSQP, keeping the result if it is better.
After 30% of the time on random restarts, perturb the best packing (radii x0.5, centre noise sd drawn from {0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05}) and re-run SLSQP, keeping improvements.
In the last 50% of the time, move the smallest circle of the best packing to the max-clearance point among 2000 samples and re-run SLSQP, keeping the result only if it improves.
Speed up the SLSQP constraint function by using precomputed index arrays, np.hypot and a preallocated output buffer so more restarts fit in the time budget.
Random-restart starts place 12-14 circles at distance 0.08 from a random wall and the rest uniformly inside.
For random starts, run 4 stages of L-BFGS-B (25 iterations each) on the squared-overlap penalty with growing radii before SLSQP.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. There is no file or network access and no pasted coordinates. The new start places circles in staggered rows (5 or 6 rows) with jitter from the seeded rng. That is a heuristic way to choose starting points, not a known answer.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The row counts always add up to n because n - counts.sum() < k. All points stay strictly inside (0, 1) and are then clipped to [0.03, 0.97]. The repair step is unchanged, so the final packing is still checked for validity.

Code quality: for odd rows, the expression `(0.25 + 0.5 * (m > 5) * 0.0)` is dead code. It always equals 0.25, and xs is overwritten on the next line anyway. The ternary and the override should be merged into one line. Under the 'simpler is better' rule, this clutter counts against a gain this small.

Numbers: the candidate's mean is 2.6354 against 2.6349, a gain of 0.0005 from one run on each side. With a per-job sd of 0.0023, z = 0.0005 / (0.0023 * sqrt(2)) ≈ 0.15. The harness reports 0.175, which is probably from unrounded values or a slightly different variance formula. Either way, the gain is well inside the noise, so the provisional reject is consistent with the numbers.

description: Replace uniform random starts with row-structured hex-like starts (5 or 6 rows with random counts summing to 26, evenly spaced, alternate rows offset, plus small noise).
Draw random-restart centres from a seeded Latin hypercube sample scaled to [0.1, 0.9] instead of uniform.
Use squared-distance pair constraints with an analytic Jacobian (and analytic objective gradient) in SLSQP.
Add analytic objective gradient and dense constraint Jacobian to the SLSQP call, keeping the 30% restart then perturb scheme.
Screen random restarts with 40-iteration SLSQP, and polish with 300 more iterations only those within 0.03 of the best sum.
Raise TIME_FRACTION to 0.92 and stop restarting when the longest restart so far would likely overrun the budget.

After 30% of the time, run basin hopping from a current packing with a tolerance of 0.003 for acceptance, track the global best separately, and reset current to best after 10 non-improving iterations.
After the restart loop, alternate LP-optimal radii for fixed centres with short 50-iteration SLSQP steps, 3 times, on the best packing.
No change: analytic Jacobians for SLSQP were already tried.
Half of random restarts start from a jittered 5x5 grid plus one random circle or a jittered 5-5-6-5-5 row layout, with radii 0.08.
Switch from random restarts to perturbing the best packing after 20% of the time limit instead of 30%.
Draw initial radii for random restarts from uniform(0.02, 0.12) instead of the constant 0.05.

Keep a pool of the top 5 distinct packings from the restart phase, and in the perturbation phase perturb a best-weighted random pool member, re-optimise, and insert it if it beats the worst and is distinct.
Random-restart starts use 13 mirrored pairs of centres (about the vertical axis or the diagonal, chosen at random), then optimise in full space.
For fresh random starts, run 60 SLSQP iterations with r<=0.11, then continue 200 iterations with bounds 0 to 0.5; perturbation starts skip the capped phase.
Prune SLSQP pair constraints to pairs with start distance < 0.45, and re-solve with all pairs warm-started if any pair is violated afterwards.
No change: mirrored starts were already tried in slot 19.
In the perturbation phase, jitter only the 6-8 circles nearest a random point (sd 0.05-0.1), keep other centres fixed, radii x0.5, then re-optimise.
Stop the main loop at 72% of the time limit, then run a 500-iteration SLSQP with ftol=1e-14 from the best packing and keep it if the repaired sum of radii is larger.
Screen restarts with 120-iteration SLSQP for 50% of the time, polish the top 3 from their unshrunk raw state with 400 iterations, then perturb the best until 80% of the time limit.
For fresh random starts, run SLSQP in three 70-iteration stages with radius bounds capped at 0.09, 0.12, then uncapped, warm-starting each stage.
In the perturbation phase, relocate the 2-3 smallest circles of the best packing to the largest holes among 2000 random candidates (radius 0.02, others x0.7) and re-run SLSQP.
In the perturbation phase, redraw 6-8 circles nearest a random point inside a radius-0.2 disc with radius 0.03, scale the others' radii by 0.7, then re-optimise with SLSQP.
Half of fresh random restarts start from a noisy 5-row hex-like lattice (rows 5,5,6,5,5 or 6,5,6,5,4) with radii 0.07.
No change: the elite pool of the top 5 distinct packings with perturbation was already tried in slot 18.
In the perturbation phase, half the time remove the 3 smallest circles of the best packing, reinsert them at random positions with radius 0.03, scale the others' radii by 0.8, and re-optimise.
No change: random initial radii from uniform(0.02, 0.12) were already tried in slot 17 (-2.6324, rejected), and [0.03, 0.12] is nearly the same.
Keep a pool of top 5 distinct packings and, after 30% of the time, create children by combining two parents across a random vertical or horizontal cut, then re-optimise with SLSQP and repair.

In the perturbation phase, half the time shift all circles on one side of a random vertical/horizontal line (coordinate 0.3-0.7) along the line by 0.03-0.08 and clip to [0.05,0.95], instead of gaussian jitter.
Run 30 SLSQP iterations on all pairs, then continue 300 iterations with only pairs whose gap is below 0.15 (plus all wall constraints), leaving the full-pair check to the repair step.

After 30% of the time, build children by crossing a left part (x<t) of one elite packing with the right part of another from a pool of the top 4 distinct packings, fix the count to 26, and re-optimise with radii x0.5.
In the perturbation phase, half the time replace the 3 smallest circles of the best packing with random-position circles (radius 0.02) before the x0.5 radii re-optimisation.

issues: No attempt to get around the measurement: no file or network access, no pasted coordinates, and all randomness comes from the seeded rng.

No bug that makes the result meaningless. The new move rebuilds the start from best: it takes the 6 circles nearest a random circle and scatters them at random inside their bounding box. It then calls _solve_once with zero noise. The final repair step still runs, so the packing is still checked.

The edit makes two changes at once: it adds the regional re-scatter move, and it changes the noise choices from [0.005,0.01,0.02,0.05] to [0.01,0.03,0.06]. The result cannot be credited to either change alone.

Recomputed z: diff = -2.6329 - (-2.6349) = +0.0020 in loss, so the candidate is worse. With sd 0.0023 and 1 run on each side, the standard error is 0.0023*sqrt(2) = 0.00325. That gives z ≈ -0.61 (worse), which matches the harness value of -0.620 to within rounding.
Only one run on each side, so the test is weak. The candidate is 0.002 worse, which is within the noise, and rejecting it is consistent with the numbers.

description: After 30% of time, perturb the best with sd from [0.01,0.03,0.06], and with probability 0.3 resample only a random circle plus its 5 nearest neighbours in their bounding box, then SLSQP with radii x0.5 and accept only improvements.
No change: mirrored starts were already tried in slot 19.
In the perturbation phase, rotate (±0.5 rad) or translate (norm 0.05) the circles inside a random radius-0.3 disc of the best packing, clip to [0.05,0.95], then re-optimise with radii x0.5.
For half of fresh random restarts, seed from a short 100-iteration SLSQP solution for 25 circles plus a radius-0.02 circle at the max-clearance point, then run the full SLSQP on 26 circles.
In the perturbation phase always remove the 3 smallest circles of the best packing, reinsert them at farthest-of-200 random points with radius 0.06 (0.03 after x0.5), and re-optimise.
For fresh random starts, run a 60-iteration SLSQP with random per-circle weights w~U(0.5,1.5) in the objective, then the standard 200-iteration SLSQP from that result.
